review.summary: Attempt 2 closes every prior finding with real changes, not prose: README now names 0.2.3 as the verified published release (bound by tools/test_release_024.py:31-35), PHASES.md gained a phase-28 acceptance paragraph, CI.md documents the actual --resume set and phase-28 exclusion, RELEASE.md adds the complete 0.2.4 delivery commands, check-access-release.py:68 is a single call, check_phase.py:898 derives its diagnostic from CONTRACT_CI_PHASES, and check-dependencies.py now independently audits the native-probes lockfile with fail-closed coverage. Evidence is genuinely executed: 105 commands, all exit 0, one continuous 13:31-14:02 run on source 63009ca5, including both --require-directional clean packages (392s/377s) that ran the directional example in-archive and as an external consumer on 1.89.0 and 1.99.0. Residual issues are documentation/policy-scope lows.

findings.description: The canonical dependency-policy section still describes a single lockfile ("the unchanged lockfile", line 103) and says the checker "verifies registry checksums and permits only crates.io dependency sources". After this chunk, scripts/check-dependencies.py:127-152 independently audits contracts/native-probes/Cargo.lock and records lockfileAudits (docs/checks/phase-28-dependencies.json:56,102), while check_lock/check_policy and cargo-deny still cover only the SDK graph. That split is stated only inside the receipt's limitations array (scripts/check-dependencies.py:247). CHANGELOG.md:44-47 likewise mentions only the root lockfile refresh, although contracts/native-probes/Cargo.lock:1123,1772 were updated to the same patched versions.
findings.required_fix: Document the dual-lockfile advisory audit and the SDK-only license/source/checksum scope in docs/DEPENDENCIES.md, note the probe-lockfile refresh in CHANGELOG.md, and add docs/DEPENDENCIES.md to this chunk's scope_evidence.

findings.description: check_lock and check_policy are applied only to the root lockfile (lock_path = ROOT/'Cargo.lock', lines 164-168). A git/path source or a dependency without a registry checksum added to contracts/native-probes/Cargo.lock would still pass the phase-28 dependency gate, even though that lockfile is compiled by the external package consumers (scripts/check-package.py:187,196-206) and by the native-probes CI feature set. The new audit_lockfiles only runs cargo-audit against it.
findings.required_fix: Call check_lock on tomllib.loads(contracts/native-probes/Cargo.lock) as well, or state the deliberate exclusion in docs/DEPENDENCIES.md and docs/CI.md.

findings.description: The directional binding checks the archive member digest, the working-tree digest, selectedFeatures == [], uniqueness against indices/frozenProbeCheckIndex, the command, and the cwd, but nothing in the recorded check row identifies which example source was copied into the consumer's src/main.rs. The directional external run (docs/checks/phase-28-release-package-1.99.0.json:1087-1101) is byte-identical in command and cwd to the access-policy run; the claim that checkIndex 17 is the directional run rests on the producer script's hash bindings (packageScriptSha256/wrapperSha256) rather than on the receipt row itself.
findings.required_fix: Record the consumer main.rs digest (or assert the expected stdout line) per external-consumer check row in scripts/check-package.py:218-223 and verify it in verify_receipt, so the directional run is self-identifying.

evidence: Prior findings are resolved in source, not claimed: README.md:33-35,59-61 name 0.2.3 as "the current verified published version" with a link to docs/checks/release-registry-0.2.3.json and drop the old 0.2.0 install line; tools/test_release_024.py:31-35 binds those exact strings. docs/PHASES.md:291-303 is the new phase-28 acceptance paragraph (asserted at test_release_024.py:37-38). docs/CI.md:327,338-339 state the real --resume set and that phase 28 forbids checkpoint reuse, matching tools/check_phase.py:893,895. docs/RELEASE.md:208-253 adds the full 0.2.4 sequence (cargo +1.99.0 publish, verify-publication with both proofs, observe-release tag/ci, release_delivery --phase 28), asserted at test_release_024.py:42-51. scripts/check-access-release.py:68 is now one call with require_directional=phase == 28. tools/check_phase.py:898 derives the diagnostic from CONTRACT_CI_PHASES, asserted at test_release_024.py:89-97.

Check evidence is complete and current-source bound: docs/reviews/phase-28-chunk-release-readiness-attempt-02.checks.json:1-6 records phase 28, source_sha256 63009ca5..., source_unchanged true, passed true; 105 "exit_code" entries with zero non-zero values and no "timeout": true. tools/review_phase.py:222-228 requires [item['command'] for item in checks] == commands_for(28) with every exit_code == 0, and :232-233 re-verifies checkpoint_bindings for phase 28 against current bytes. docs/checks/phase-28.json:2-6 carries the identical header; no docs/checks/phase-28-partial.json exists and tools/check_phase.py:895 rejects --resume for phase 28.

The run is real and continuous, not assembled: first check executed_at 2026-10-22T13:31:26, last (check-access-release) 14:02:26, with heavy steps at 392.551s and 376.633s for the two package qualifications and nineteen further commands over 19-87s (checks.json:1021-2855).

The three phase-28-specific guards executed: checks.json:2862-2891 and 2893-2923 are scripts/check-management-package.py --require-directional for 1.89.0 and 1.99.0, each with checkpoint_bindings to its receipt and to the retained .crate under .local/package-worktrees/17c994619d913e96c35b0b5fb049a4e1a02bc083/; :2924-2955 is check-access-release.py --phase 28 --version 0.2.4 returning version 0.2.4, releaseCommit 17c9946..., archiveSha256 9683a688..., toolchains [1.89.0, 1.99.0]. tools/check_phase.py:319-328 defines exactly that set as commands_for(27) renamed plus these three.

--require-directional is a substantive constraint with negative coverage: scripts/check-management-package.py:114 demands exactly 5 external consumer indices (4 otherwise) and :152-164 requires the archived examples/directional_profiles.rs, digest equality with the working tree, selectedFeatures == [], a unique in-range checkIndex running in the external consumer root, and a separate in-archive run --example directional_profiles --all-features --locked --offline. tools/test_release_024.py:240-268 rejects a wrong sha256, a checkIndex colliding with frozenProbeCheckIndex, selectedFeatures == ['red-team'], and omission of the entry.

Both compilers actually executed the directional consumer on this source: docs/checks/phase-28-release-package-1.99.0.json:4-8,767-771,1087-1101 (schemaVersion 3, rustc 1.99.0, selectedFeatures [], stdout "Directional typed models and lossless response compatibility verified offline.") and phase-28-release-package-1.89.0.json:4-6,770,979,1099 (rustc 1.89.0, both the in-archive example and the external consumer). Both receipts carry sourceSha256 63009ca5... (:1108) and releaseCommit 17c9946..., and contracts/native-probes/Cargo.toml:11 supplies the management feature so selectedFeatures == [] is meaningful.

The example is a real consumer of the new API, not a stub: crates/scm-sdk/examples/directional_profiles.rs:13-32 builds ContentTypeConfiguration/ContentTypeConfigurations, enable_full_conversation_inspection(false), content_type_mode and dlp_tenant_id "100"; :34-49 round-trips through typescript:0.35.0:CreateSecurityProfileRequestSchema and asserts the hyphenated wire keys; :50-57 asserts lossless preservation of a wrong-typed/null response in Mode::Response and Mode::ResponseWithoutDefaults.

The dual-lockfile audit ran and fails closed: scripts/check-dependencies.py:127-152 audits Cargo.lock and contracts/native-probes/Cargo.lock at one pinned RustSec revision with --no-fetch --deny warnings and re-checks each digest; docs/checks/phase-28-dependencies.json:3-13,56,98-102,144-145 shows the audit at 13:34:07 against revision 640bf5a9 with freshHead true and both lockfiles passed/unchanged. tools/test_dependency_policy.py:22-71 exercises clean/advisory/warning/exit/malformed/missing-warnings/changed scenarios on the probe lockfile plus a missing-file case, asserting exactly two commands with the pinned --db.

Privacy and live evidence are current, not inherited: docs/checks/phase-28-private-material.json:3-12 records a scan at 13:31:26 with sourceSha256 63009ca5..., headCommit 17c9946..., 2412 git-visible files, 135 packaged candidates, 0 credential and 0 registration matches, and scripts/check-private-material.py:206-214 rebinds it to the current source fingerprint. contracts/live-evidence.json:4-5 binds docs/checks/phase-28-live-attempt-01.json, whose runtimeInputsSha256 must equal tools/live_evidence.py:122-133 runtime_fingerprint (SDK src/examples/manifests only), so documentation-only edits legitimately preserve it; the report (:27,32-33,36-74) shows crateVersion 0.2.4, mutationsEnabled false, cleanupState not_needed, 1 verified OAuth probe and four HTTP 403 permission prerequisites.

Release claims stay bounded and unpublished: CHANGELOG.md:9-13,50-51 ("Release candidate: not yet published", establishes no publication or remote delivery), docs/STABILITY.md:7-9,32-49 (documents both validation directions: current request roots reject newly known wrong-type/null values while response paths keep frozen tolerant acceptance), docs/DIRECTIONAL_PROFILES.md:7-11, docs/LIVE_ACCEPTANCE.md:15-23 ("Directional profile create/update remain live-unverified"), contracts/qualification.json:58-60 (liveVerified 1, liveNotVerified 447).

Readiness cannot complete the phase and delivery fails closed: tools/review_phase.py:459-460 forbids --release-readiness with --advance, :478-479 rejects advancement when review_scope != "phase", and :483-489 calls release_delivery.verify(..., phase=28, version="0.2.4"). tools/release_delivery.py:22,190 register and enforce (28,'0.2.4'); :200-204 require the canonical registry/tag receipts and a docs/checks/phase-28-remote-ci-run-N.json; :226-231 forward require_directional=True and verify the retained registry archive; :104-115 require CI job contexts to equal the derived matrix exactly (49 = 24 features x 2 toolchains + contracts-and-package) with no duplicate target_urls. tools/test_release_024.py:109-137 proves both the readiness and phase paths leave docs/phase-status.json unmodified.

Version-specific guards reject cross-version reuse: scripts/check-access-release.py:30 registers (28,'0.2.4') and not (24,'0.2.4'); scripts/check-prepublication.py:19-27 accepts only {(24,'0.2.3'),(28,'0.2.4')} and re-reads readiness after the candidate check; scripts/verify-publication.py:56-69,240-243 require a phase-28 readiness review for 0.2.4 and pass require_directional=True; tools/test_release_024.py:53-61,78-87 assert the defaults and that no network call happens without a readiness review.

Governance regressions executed rather than merely registered (from the recorded stderr): test_review_phase.py 52 tests OK, test_management_phases.py 27 OK, test_red_team_management.py 51 OK, test_management_consumers.py 7 OK, test_management_fixtures.py 4 OK, test_red_team_management_models.py 13 OK, plus verify-contracts.py --self-test rejecting 29 named tampering cases and red_team_management.py --check --current-source-compatibility reporting current-source bounded reads with "release acceptance not assessed".

Scope bookkeeping is immutable and correct: docs/phase-status.json:7891-8085 keeps from_attempt 1 and from_attempt 2 revisions, the attempt-2 revision adding tools/test_dependency_policy.py and equalling the live scope (required by tools/review_phase.py:244-261); docs/reviews/phase-28-chunk-release-readiness-attempt-01.json:91-183 retains the narrower attempt-1 list. tools/test_typescript035_governance.py:208-226 proves all pre-26 phase records are byte-identical to 578f2e6 and that phase 28 is final in this sequence. Glob by modification time shows the most recently changed sources (test_ci.py, test_dependency_policy.py, check-dependencies.py, test_release_024.py, check_phase.py, check-access-release.py, README.md, docs/RELEASE.md, docs/CI.md, docs/PHASES.md) are all inside the declared scope.
limitations: Read-only review: I executed no commands and re-ran nothing. All pass/fail conclusions rest on reading docs/reviews/phase-28-chunk-release-readiness-attempt-02.checks.json (105 commands, header identical to docs/checks/phase-28.json) and tracing tools/check_phase.py:319-328 against tools/review_phase.py:201-234. I did not recompute the source fingerprint, the checks-file digest fe64ca83..., any receipt SHA-256, or the retained .crate digests.

I did not open the retained archives under .local/package-worktrees/17c9946.../.local/artifacts/ or the extracted consumer roots; directional consumer execution is established by the recorded receipts plus the verification logic in scripts/check-management-package.py:152-164 and the recorded stdout, not by inspecting build output.

Remote delivery is the other phase-28 chunk and is unverified here: no docs/checks/release-registry-0.2.4.json, release-tag-v0.2.4.json or phase-28-remote-ci-run-N.json exists, docs/phase-status.json:8249-8259 milestones are all pending with no registry_publication block for phase 28, and the 49 CI contexts have not been observed on the released source. I judged only that the guards for that evidence exist and fail closed. Equally, the phase-scope release-readiness review (docs/reviews/phase-28-attempt-01.json, rejected) must still be re-obtained and pass before publication.

Generated model correctness, the additive overlay, the oracle corpus and the schema-graph roots are accepted phase-27 deliverables; I relied on this phase's recorded compiler/package/fixture receipts and declaration-level documentation rather than re-auditing crates/scm-sdk/src/models/generated.rs or src/validation/schema_graph.json.

Per instruction I read no credential or tenant-registration files, nothing outside this repository, and no optional .local/typescript checkout; the verify-contracts.py --baseline .local/typescript result (extractedBaselineVerified true) is taken from the recorded run.

Phase 24/25 acceptance, the published 0.2.3 delivery gate and pre-phase-26 release infrastructure were out of scope beyond the pinned 0.2.3 receipt identity enforced at tools/review_phase.py:409-413 and the published-0.2.3 facts relevant to the closed README finding.
